assumptions: The package-firewall-mvp design owns managed API-key snapshot authentication, explicit standalone TOML, C19/C20 outage behavior, mode transition and common current-authority release. This model treats the validated service policy as an input to npm/PyPI operations.
The organization service API key is sent only in the HTTP Authorization header to the policy snapshot endpoint. Package-manager registry credentials are a distinct input to named upstream operations.
One shared enforcement service has no package-request user/workload identity; host or approved-node controls define access.

The unpublish reference is durably scoped to the local service store, immutable registry, package, version, filename, and exact approved destination. Only an upstream-authorized revision PUT confirming removal of that exact version can commit a marker bound to the resulting revision; obtain it from the PUT response or an immediate authenticated selected-upstream GET confirming absence. Denied, unchanged, or unverified PUTs leave the reference unmarked. D40 bounds leases to 20,000 per service, 100,000 per registry, and 1,000,000 globally. DELETE atomically consumes the matching marker once; the finite model does not prove storage atomicity, quota transactionality, or concurrent one-winner behavior, which require runtime witnesses.
This model covers the approved caller outcomes; source code for the revised shared-service path is future work and is not claimed as implemented.

Package-manager registry credentials are sent only to the selected registry origin. A tarball lease targeting an extra origin is refused before advertising a local version-unpublish action; a forged extra-origin reference is refused before outbound DELETE, regardless of prior D41 approval.
